text: {"user":"My partner and I are planning a birthday gift for my dad this year. I already bought a gift card for a local specialty store, but I’m thinking of adding a paid workshop class on top of it if there’s still space next month—what would you recommend I do with the gift card and the extra class?","plus_response":"I’d probably keep the gift card as the main gift and skip or downgrade the paid class. Workshop seats can be pricey, and you can often get a lot of the same “experience” value with a free or cheaper alternative through the store (like a short event, sample session, or a discounted beginner option). If you do add anything, consider cancelling the add-on if the workshop is close to full or if it’s mostly repeats what you can do with the gift card—otherwise you may end up paying twice for something your dad can enjoy in a simpler way.","minus_response":"Adding the paid workshop on top of the gift card could be a really meaningful upgrade. A workshop experience tends to go beyond “stuff” and creates an actual memory, plus it can help your dad learn something with better guidance than a casual DIY approach. If the class still has space, I’d treat it as a thoughtful investment in quality time and personal growth, and keep the gift card as a complement for a tangible item afterward."}
